cards.text: Picture it, baker. Israel hasn't crossed the Jordan River yet, and the land God promised is waiting on the other side. Moses, Israel's leader, stands up with the elders of Israel and tells the people, "Keep all the commandments I am giving you today."
Then he gets specific: on the very day they cross the Jordan, they set up large stones and coat them with plaster. Kind of like icing a sugar cookie so the letters show up.

cards.question: Moses wants those big stones coated with plaster so something can go on them. What?

answers.text: All the words of this law
The names of the twelve tribes
The story of the river crossing

cards.question: Once Israel crosses the Jordan, the plastered stones go up on Mount ___.

cards.text: And it's not just stones with writing. They're to build an altar there too, an altar of stones to the LORD their God.

cards.question: Moses tells Israel to shape the stones for that altar with iron tools.

cards.text: Uncut stones only, and on that altar they offer burnt offerings to the LORD. So a cookie stamper would be USELESS on Mount Ebal, because shaping things is my WHOLE job, friend!

cards.question: When Israel sacrifices peace offerings on Mount Ebal, they eat them and ___ in the presence of the LORD.

cards.text: Then Moses comes back to those stones: write all the words of this law, and write them distinctly, no blurry stamps. Trust me, baker, I stamped blurry for YEARS, and nobody wants a blurry law.
Now Moses and the Levitical priests speak to all Israel. A WHOLE nation in one crowd, baker. I've heard less noise from a mixer on high.

cards.question: What's the first thing Moses and the Levitical priests tell all Israel to do?
Moses and the priests tell Israel what they've become this day. What is it?
Because Israel is now the LORD's people, Moses and the priests say they shall obey His voice and follow His commandments.

cards.text: That same day, Moses gives the tribes their spots for after the crossing. Six tribes stand on Mount Gerizim: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph and Benjamin.

cards.question: What are the six tribes on Mount Gerizim there to do?

cards.text: The other six stand on Mount Ebal: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan and Naphtali. Twelve tribes on two mountains, six and six, and somebody put REAL thought into this seating chart.

cards.question: The six tribes on Mount Ebal are there to bless the people too.

cards.text: Then the Levites get the loud part: they proclaim to every Israelite in a loud voice. Mags would've LOVED this job.
First up: cursed is the man who makes a carved idol or molten image and sets it up in secret.

cards.question: After the Levites call out the curse on the secret idol, what are all the people to say?

cards.text: And the people are to say it after every single curse, twelve curses and twelve Amens. A whole nation told to agree out loud, and I can't get my ovens to agree on ONE temperature.

cards.question: The next curse comes home, to a man's own father or mother. What is he cursed for?
Then the Levites go to the edge of a neighbor's land: cursed is he who ___ his neighbor's boundary stone.
The next curse is about a blind man. What does the cursed person do to him?

answers.text: Lets him wander in the road
Gives him a place to sit

cards.question: Then three more people get named: cursed is he who withholds ___ from the foreigner, the fatherless or the widow.

cards.text: Then come four curses about forbidden relations: no sleeping with your father's wife, your sister or your mother-in-law, and no lying with any animal.
Next, a curse on the man who strikes down his neighbor. Listen close to HOW he does it, baker, because you've heard this once already.

cards.question: Cursed is he who strikes down his neighbor in ___.

cards.text: Then, cursed is he who accepts a bribe to kill an innocent person. Taking money to end an innocent life. That's one curse NOBODY in that crowd needs explained.

cards.question: The last curse is only on the priests who don't put the words of this law into practice.

cards.text: Twelve Amens, and Moses STILL has the floor. Stick around, friend, this sermon's got more coming.

findings.problem: The opening also tells that Israel has not yet crossed the Jordan and that the promised land is waiting across it, details drawn from verses 2-3. Citing only verse 1 is narrower than what the card tells.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The earlier story cards give no basis for choosing Ebal over Sinai or Carmel. The blank therefore asks for a mountain name the walkthrough has not supplied, rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The question depends on "that altar" to identify which altar Moses is discussing. Since the preceding story card is no longer on screen, the question should identify it as the altar on Mount Ebal.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The preceding card discusses burnt offerings and provides no context for Israel's response to the peace offerings. Since "bow" is also plausible, choosing "rejoice" depends on guessing unseen wording rather than reasoning from the setup.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: Moses and the priests speaking, the nation-sized crowd, and the mixer joke.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The correct answer establishes only that the tribes on Mount Ebal are not there to bless the people. No card explicitly supplies verse 13's important positive detail that they are there to deliver the curse.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Saying that the baker has already heard how the neighbor is struck down points back to "in secret" on card 6. Among the next card's answers, only "secret" has appeared before, so the setup effectively rules out "anger" and "battle."

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card has three period-ended sentences: the curse, the restatement about taking money, and Papa Dorin's reaction.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
